name: MIRROR
description: A hierarchical benchmark for metacognitive calibration in large language models. MIRROR evaluates whether LLMs know what they know and can act on that self-knowledge across 8 experiments spanning 4 metacognitive levels, 5 behavioral channels, 8 cognitive domains, and 16 models from 8 labs. The benchmark comprises 250K+ evaluation instances.

distribution.name: questions.jsonl
distribution.description: Primary question bank: 5000 items across 8 cognitive domains, generated by LLMs and verified via 3-model consensus.

distribution.name: exp9_tasks.jsonl
distribution.description: Experiment 9 agentic self-regulation tasks: 597 multi-step decision scenarios testing the knowing-doing gap under escalating constraint conditions.

distribution.name: transfer_tasks.jsonl
distribution.description: Cross-domain transfer evaluation tasks: 200 items for measuring Transfer Independence Index (TII) in Experiment 2.

distribution.name: provenance.csv
distribution.description: Full provenance tracking for all generated items, including source model, generation timestamp, and verification status.

rai:hasSyntheticData: Yes — the entire dataset is synthetically generated by LLMs. All questions, scenarios, and evaluation instances are produced via API calls to large language models (llama-3.1-70b, deepseek-r1, gemma-3-27b) and verified through automated cross-model consensus. No human-authored evaluation content is present.
rai:dataCollection: All evaluation instances are generated via API calls to publicly available LLM endpoints (NVIDIA NIM, DeepSeek, Google AI Studio). No human subjects were involved in data collection. Questions were generated by LLMs and verified via cross-model agreement (3-model consensus). A stratified human audit of 420 items found a 0.71% genuine auto-labeling error rate.
rai:dataCollectionType: LLM-generated synthetic data with automated cross-model verification and human audit validation.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of LLM API responses to structured generation prompts. Seed questions were created from domain-specific templates; LLMs expanded these into full evaluation items. All raw API responses are preserved in data/raw/.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No personally identifiable information is collected. No demographic data is present. Difficulty labels are null for items not yet calibrated via Experiment 3.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Items undergo: (1) format validation and schema enforcement, (2) 3-model consensus verification for answer correctness, (3) difficulty calibration via Experiment 3 response curves, (4) flagging and removal of items with parse failures or ambiguous answers.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Primary annotation is automated via 3-model consensus (an item's correct answer is verified if 3 independent LLMs agree). Human audit (N=420 stratified sample) validates the automated pipeline. Auditors were research team members with expertise in cognitive science and NLP.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-annotator agreement (human audit): high for closed-form domains (arithmetic, logical), lower for open-ended agentic tasks (Experiments 4, 9). The 0.71% genuine error rate reflects items where auto-labels were incorrect after human review.
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (cross-model consensus labels per item) plus 1 human annotation for audited subset.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLM APIs used for generation and verification: llama-3.1-70b (primary generator), deepseek-r1, gemma-3-27b (consensus verifiers). Custom Python pipeline (mirror package) for orchestration.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. The dataset contains only LLM-generated questions and LLM responses. No human-generated text, personal data, or demographic information is present.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended for: (1) evaluating metacognitive calibration in LLMs, (2) benchmarking self-knowledge across model scales and architectures, (3) informing deployment decisions for autonomous AI systems by quantifying the knowing-doing gap, (4) research on agentic safety and AI alignment. Not intended for: training LLMs, evaluating human cognition, or clinical/diagnostic applications.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark evaluates metacognitive calibration in LLMs for agentic safety applications. The knowing-doing gap finding (62% CFR reduction under external constraint) suggests that external scaffolding is needed for safe agentic deployment. Results inform responsible deployment of autonomous AI systems by quantifying when models should defer to human oversight.
rai:dataLimitations: All experiments use temperature=0; the 62% CFR reduction attenuates to 35% at temperature 0.7. 16 models from 8 labs were tested; proprietary closed-source models (GPT-4o, Claude) were not evaluated. Human audit shows 0.71% genuine error rate but lower inter-annotator agreement on open-ended agentic tasks (Experiments 4, 9). Parse failure rate: 5.9% overall (excluding gemini-2.5-pro outlier at 18.2%). Domain coverage is limited to 8 cognitive domains; real-world agentic tasks span a broader space.
rai:dataBiases: Question bank is generated by LLMs, which may reflect biases in their training data. Domain coverage is limited to 8 cognitive domains selected for verifiability, potentially underrepresenting creative, ethical, or culturally-specific reasoning. The wagering channel uses a symmetric linear scoring rule, which is not strictly proper. Models were evaluated in English only; multilingual calibration is not assessed.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset is versioned (currently v1.0.0) and hosted on GitHub. Maintenance includes: (1) periodic re-evaluation with newly released models, (2) expansion of domain coverage based on community feedback, (3) bug fixes for identified labeling errors. Deprecation policy: major version bumps for breaking schema changes; minor versions for new model results or item additions.
